equation: dX = -X**5 * dt,   X(0) = xi ~ Normal(0, sigma_bar**2)
diffusion_derivative: g(X) = 0 (noise-free; the only randomness is the Gaussian initial condition). dg/dX = 0.
milstein_correction: 0 (no diffusion term; Milstein == Euler-Maruyama == deterministic per-path ODE integration).

analytic_moments.derivation: Per-path exact solution of dX=-X^5 dt is X_t = xi / (1 + 4 t xi^4)^(1/4). Mean E[X_T] = 0 by odd symmetry (X_T is an odd function of the symmetric Gaussian xi). Variance = E[X_T^2] = integral over xi ~ N(0, sigma_bar^2) of xi^2 / (1 + 4 t xi^4)^(1/2). This is an exact 1D Gaussian integral with no elementary closed form; evaluate by quadrature. At T=1, sigma_bar=1/3 the value is 0.09248275891 (compare E[X_0^2] = sigma_bar^2 = 0.11111...).

implementation_notes: Noise-free (deterministic) Ito SDE with a random Gaussian initial condition; Monte Carlo is over xi only, there is NO Wiener increment. State is scalar (d=1) and the drift f(X) = -X^5 is strongly superlinear (stiff). Naive explicit Euler-Maruyama y_{n+1} = y_n - y_n^5 * dt overshoots and blows up (double-exponentially) on paths with large |xi|; do NOT use plain explicit EM. Use a tamed scheme (divide the drift by 1 + dt*|drift|, i.e. y_{n+1} = y_n - (y_n^5 * dt)/(1 + dt*|y_n^5|)), an adaptive step, or an implicit/semi-implicit integrator. Since each path is a deterministic ODE, integrating the exact per-path formula X_T = xi/(1+4T xi^4)^(1/4) is also valid. Exact mean is 0 (near-zero -> mean check is skipped via near_zero_mean_threshold). Exact variance at T=1 is 0.09248275891, obtained from the Gaussian quadrature in variance_expression.
